claims.text: Edge video object detection faces high energy costs due to repeated detector invocations on temporally redundant frames.
claims.poster_quote: Edge video object detection faces high energy costs due to repeated detector invocations on temporally redundant frames.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Video object detection on edge devices requires running computationally expensive detectors over long frame streams, leading to high energy consumption and sustained GPU utilization.
claims.reason: Section I, Introduction: The paper explicitly states that edge video object detection faces high energy costs due to repeated detector invocations.

claims.text: Naive frame-skipping (e.g., FixedSkip-2) causes severe accuracy loss of 8.6 percentage points in AP@50 by skipping during critical events like object entry or motion.
claims.poster_quote: Naive frame-skipping (e.g., FixedSkip-2) causes severe accuracy loss (8.6 pp AP@50 drop) by skipping during critical events like object entry or motion.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Fixed-cadence skipping (the simplest content-blind baseline studied in prior work [22]–[24]) drops accuracy sharply: on the BDD100K MOT [11], skipping every second frame loses 8.6 pp AP@50 (average precision at IoU 0.5; 14% relative).
claims.reason: Section I, Introduction: The paper provides the exact numerical accuracy loss for FixedSkip-2, supporting the claim.

claims.text: Existing adaptive methods require detector retraining, depend on codecs, or fail under ego-motion.
claims.poster_quote: Existing adaptive methods are insufficient: they require detector retraining, depend on codecs, or fail under ego-motion.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Adaptive alternatives exist [3], [4], [24]–[31], but no existing approach simultaneously provides the properties needed for drop-in edge deployment: detector-agnostic operation, no detector retraining, codec-free execution, ego-motion robustness, and demonstrated energy efficiency on commercial edge SoCs.
claims.reason: Section I, Introduction: The paper explicitly lists the limitations of existing adaptive methods, supporting the claim.

claims.text: ALBIREO enables detector-agnostic, codec-free, content-aware skipping using per-object temporal state.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO fills this gap by enabling detector-agnostic, codec-free, content-aware skipping using per-object temporal state.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We present ALBIREO, a detector-agnostic, codec-free, adaptive inference framework that wraps off-the-shelf object detectors and decides when detector invocation can be safely skipped based on scene content and per-object temporal state.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly describes ALBIREO as detector-agnostic, codec-free, and content-aware.

claims.text: ALBIREO wraps off-the-shelf detectors with a forward-looking uncertainty trigger that uses a 10D Kalman filter per object and skips detection when predicted covariance trace is below threshold u.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO wraps off-the-shelf detectors with three mechanisms: 1) Forward-looking uncertainty trigger: Uses 10D Kalman filter per object; skips detection when predicted covariance trace is below threshold u, avoiding stale comparisons.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: To judge when skipping is safe, ALBIREO maintains a 10-dimensional Kalman filter (KF) for each active object state and invokes the detector only when prediction uncertainty exceeds a threshold.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly describes the forward-looking uncertainty trigger using a 10D Kalman filter.

claims.text: ALBIREO wraps off-the-shelf detectors with a detector-flicker rescue mechanism that emits Kalman-predicted boxes for unmatched confirmed objects if recent confidence was high and rescue cap not exceeded.
claims.poster_quote: 2) Detector-flicker rescue: On inference frames, emits Kalman-predicted boxes for unmatched confirmed objects if recent confidence was high and rescue cap not exceeded, preventing output fragmentation.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A KF-based rescue mechanism preserves confirmed object states through brief detector misses, preventing output fragmentation that degrades detection-to-ground-truth matching.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly describes the rescue mechanism and its conditions.

claims.text: ALBIREO wraps off-the-shelf detectors with an empty-scene screen mechanism that uses a lightweight ERD classifier to skip full detection on objectless frames.
claims.poster_quote: 3) Empty-scene screen: Uses lightweight ERD classifier to skip full detection on objectless frames.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A lightweight empty-scene screen further avoids full detector calls on objectless frames.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly describes the empty-scene screen mechanism.

claims.text: ALBIREO does not require detector modification or retraining.
claims.poster_quote: No detector modification or retraining needed.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: ALBIREO requires no detector modification or detector retraining and is designed as a drop-in efficiency layer for improving the accuracy–energy–latency tradeoff of edge video-detection pipelines.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly states that ALBIREO does not require detector modification or retraining.

claims.text: ALBIREO’s skip decisions are content-driven, not hardware-dependent, and skip rates are identical across Thor and Orin for the same detector.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO’s skip decisions are content-driven, not hardware-dependent: skip rates are identical across Thor/Orin for same detector.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: For a fixed detector, skip rates are identical across Thor and Orin, to within rounding.
claims.reason: Section IV-D: The paper explicitly states that skip rates are content-driven and identical across platforms for the same detector.

claims.text: Energy savings vary by platform due to GPU/CPU power characteristics.
claims.poster_quote: Energy savings vary by platform due to GPU/CPU power characteristics.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Energy savings vary, even on the same skip pattern, because GPU savings and CPU-power responses are platform dependent.
claims.reason: Section IV-D: The paper explicitly explains the variation in energy savings by platform.

claims.text: Rescue is invoked in 43-49% of frames and is crucial for maintaining accuracy.
claims.poster_quote: Rescue is invoked in 43-49% of frames, crucial for maintaining accuracy.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: For YOLO26x, AI frames account for 48.9% of all frames, and 61% of frames where the detector runs.
claims.reason: Section IV-E: The paper explicitly states the rescue invocation rate and its importance for maintaining accuracy.

claims.text: Empty-scene screening is effective only when conditionally applied, not per-frame.
claims.poster_quote: Empty-scene screening is effective only when conditionally applied (not per-frame).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: ERD-only is a baseline that tests whether scene-level empty-frame screening is sufficient without per-object state. Even with the same BDD100K-fine-tuned ERD used by ALBIREO, running ERD on every frame yields a 7.6% skip rate, though per-clip energy increases by 28%.
claims.reason: Section IV-C: The paper explicitly states that empty-scene screening is effective only when conditionally applied.

claims.text: ALBIREO adapts per clip: dense scenes emphasize rescue for accuracy, while sparse scenes show the largest energy savings via empty-frame skipping.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO adapts per clip: dense scenes emphasize rescue for accuracy; sparse scenes show largest energy savings via empty-frame skipping.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Dense clips emphasize rescue and accuracy preservation, while sparse clips expose the largest energy savings through empty-scene skipping.
claims.reason: Section IV-H: The paper explicitly describes ALBIREO’s adaptation to clip density.

claims.text: CPU overhead is measurable on Orin but negligible on Thor’s larger CPU complex.
claims.poster_quote: CPU overhead is measurable on Orin but negligible on Thor’s larger CPU complex.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On Orin, average CPU power roughly doubles under ALBIREO from 1.6 W to 3.6 W, while CPU utilization rises from ∼7% to ∼23%. On Thor’s larger fourteen-core Neoverse V3AE CPU complex, the same operations do not increase CPU power measurably.
claims.reason: Section IV-G: The paper explicitly describes measurable CPU overhead on Orin and negligible overhead on Thor.

claims.text: ALBIREO keeps AP@50 within ±1.2 percentage points of per-frame inference while reducing energy by 12.1-17.6%.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO keeps AP@50 within ±1.2 pp of per-frame inference while reducing energy by 12.1-17.6%.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Across all evaluated detectors and platforms, ALBIREO keeps AP@50 within 1.2 pp of Vanilla per-frame inference while reducing energy by 12.1–17.6%.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly states the accuracy and energy reduction range.

claims.text: On YOLO26x, default ALBIREO improves AP@50 by +0.8 percentage points, reduces energy by 17.6% on Thor and 14.4% on Orin, and lowers EDP by 24.9% on Thor and 26.1% on Orin.
claims.poster_quote: On YOLO26x, default ALBIREO improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp, reduces energy by 17.6% (Thor) / 14.4% (Orin), and lowers EDP by 24.9% (Thor) / 26.1% (Orin).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On the primary YOLO26x configuration, ALBIREO improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp while reducing energy by 17.6% on Thor and 14.4% on Orin. It also reduces per-frame energy-delay product by 24.9% on Thor and 26.1% on Orin.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly states the default configuration results for YOLO26x.

claims.text: ALBIREO Pareto-dominates Vanilla and baselines (FixedSkip, CTD, Statues) in AP@50-EDP space for AP@50 ≥ 0.50.
claims.poster_quote: It Pareto-dominates Vanilla and baselines (FixedSkip, CTD, Statues) in AP@50-EDP space for AP@50 ≥ 0.50.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Sweeping the primary uncertainty threshold on YOLO26x traces an AP@50–EDP Pareto frontier that dominates the evaluated frame-skipping baselines (FixedSkip-N, CTD, Statues) within the target operating region (AP@50 ≥ 0.50).
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly states ALBIREO’s Pareto dominance in AP@50-EDP space.

claims.text: Rescue mechanism contributes most to AP@50 gain, achieving 0.617 versus 0.572-0.578 without rescue.
claims.poster_quote: Rescue mechanism contributes most to AP@50 gain (0.617 vs 0.572-0.578 without rescue).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Our ablation study shows that rescue is the largest AP@50 contributor among ALBIREO’s components, raising AP@50 from the no-rescue variants’ 0.572–0.578 range to 0.617.
claims.reason: Section IV-F: The paper explicitly states the rescue mechanism’s contribution to AP@50 gain.

claims.text: ALBIREO provides a practical, drop-in efficiency layer for edge video detection, improving accuracy, energy, and latency simultaneously.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO provides a practical, drop-in efficiency layer for edge video detection, improving accuracy, energy, and latency simultaneously.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: ALBIREO is designed as a drop-in efficiency layer for improving the accuracy–energy–latency tradeoff of edge video-detection pipelines.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly describes ALBIREO as a practical drop-in efficiency layer.

claims.text: Limitations of ALBIREO include potential drift under erratic motion (e.g., abrupt pedestrian moves) and domain-dependent empty-scene classifier.
claims.poster_quote: Limitations include potential drift under erratic motion (e.g., abrupt pedestrian moves) and domain-dependent empty-scene classifier.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Three limitations of the current design point to natural extensions. First, the constant-acceleration Kalman dynamics fit many vehicle-dominated dashcam scenes, but can drift under highly erratic motion, such as a pedestrian making an abrupt lateral move at a crosswalk. Second, the empty-scene screen is domain-dependent.
claims.reason: Section V-D: The paper explicitly describes these limitations.

claims.text: Future work includes learned motion residuals, adaptive rescue policies, evaluation on fixed-camera/non-driving datasets, and co-tenancy with other workloads.
claims.poster_quote: Future work: learned motion residuals, adaptive rescue policies, evaluation on fixed-camera/non-driving datasets, and co-tenancy with other workloads.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Future deployments should either fine-tune the lightweight empty-scene classifier for the target domain or replace it with a more general low-cost emptiness oracle. Adding a learned residual or class-conditioned motion model on top of the Kalman prediction is a natural extension.
claims.reason: Section V-D: The paper explicitly describes future work directions.

claims.text: ALBIREO is composable with model compression for further gains.
claims.poster_quote: Composable with model compression for further gains.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: These two directions are complementary: compression makes detector frames cheaper, and ALBIREO reduces how often those frames are executed.
claims.reason: Section V-C: The paper explicitly states ALBIREO’s composability with model compression.

claims.text: ALBIREO’s threshold sweep (u = 3 × 10^-4 to 1 × 10^-3) forms the upper Pareto frontier among evaluated systems in the AP@50 ≥ 0.50 operating region on both Jetson platforms.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO’s threshold sweep ( u = 3 × 10 -4 to 1 × 10 -3 ) forms the upper Pareto frontier among the evaluated systems in the AP@50 ≥ 0 . 50 operating region on both Jetson platforms.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Sweeping the primary uncertainty threshold on YOLO26x traces an AP@50–EDP Pareto frontier that dominates the evaluated frame-skipping baselines (FixedSkip-N, CTD, Statues) within the target operating region (AP@50 ≥ 0.50).
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly describes the threshold sweep forming the Pareto frontier.
